items.title: Lumibot: Multi-Asset Backtesting & Agentic AI Trading Framework
items.source_summary: Open-source Python framework supporting backtesting and live trading across crypto, equities, options, futures, and forex with built-in support for agentic AI strategy execution. Emphasizes safer sandbox evaluation of AI-driven trading algorithms.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's backtesting pipeline (likely in sofar/backtest/ or sofar/validation/) currently lacks integrated agentic AI strategy harness comparable to Lumibot's Agent abstraction. SOFAR's GEX calculator, options flow detector, and AI synthesis modules operate in isolation without a unified sandbox for strategy composition, multi-asset hedging validation, or live agent rollout safety frameworks. The 'safer execution' architecture is particularly absent from risk_management components.

proposed_change.change_description: Implement an Agent-centric backtesting wrapper that (1) exposes SOFAR's GEX, VIX, and options flow signals as composable strategy inputs; (2) enforces position sizing and delta-hedge validation pre-trade; (3) logs all AI synthesis decisions with confidence scores; (4) supports parallel strategy variant evaluation (e.g., different GEX thresholds, VIX term structure weightings). Add a SafetyArbiter module that rate-limits agent decisions and triggers manual review on >2σ prediction confidence or portfolio leverage breaches.
proposed_change.estimated_effort: 40-60 hours (framework design, multi-signal composition, audit logging, safety integration)

items.evidence_basis: Lumibot's 1326 GitHub stars and active maintenance demonstrate market demand for modular, multi-asset agent frameworks. SOFAR's AI pipeline lacks this abstraction layer, creating friction for strategy developers who cannot easily test signal combinations or risk constraints before deployment.
items.credibility_basis: Active GitHub project (1326 stars, 268 forks) with sustained community engagement; covers equities and options directly.
items.author: Lumiwealth

items.title: Introduction to Quantitative Finance: Multi-Factor Frameworks & AI Finance Integration
items.source_summary: Curated educational repository covering multi-factor equity quantitative frameworks (open-source teaching), academic and industry benchmarks, and AI+finance integration including LLM agents and evaluation methodologies. Emphasis on practical model benchmarking and agent evaluation.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's AI synthesis scoring methodology (sofar/ai/scoring.py or sofar/ai/ensemble.py) appears to lack formally documented benchmark evaluation routines and LLM-based signal calibration. This repository emphasizes evaluation frameworks and agent benchmarking (benchmark/evaluation), which aligns with SOFAR's need for rigorous backcheck and credibility scoring. Specifically, SOFAR's proposal backcheck module (sofar/backtest/backcheck.py) does not appear to employ multi-factor comparative analysis or LLM-augmented signal confidence assignment.

proposed_change.change_description: Integrate multi-factor benchmark evaluation: (1) Adopt comparative evaluation framework from Barca0412's curriculum to define SOFAR baseline models (e.g., simple GEX vs. GEX+VIX term structure vs. GEX+options flow); (2) Implement LLM-augmented confidence scoring where a fine-tuned LLM rates AI synthesis outputs against historical precedent and macro context; (3) Create formal benchmark_suite.py with cross-validation protocols (time-series walk-forward, rolling windows) to measure GEX accuracy, VIX prediction Sharpe ratio, and options flow signal precision. (4) Log agent decision rationale (LLM reasoning) alongside SOFAR scores for audit and credibility justification.
proposed_change.estimated_effort: 50-70 hours (benchmark architecture, LLM fine-tuning data prep, evaluation harness, comparative model validation)

items.evidence_basis: Repository emphasis on AI+finance evaluation and agent benchmarking directly addresses SOFAR's documented blind spot in methodology transparency and reproducible backcheck. The 1316 stars and 153 forks reflect community validation of the multi-factor + AI integration approach.
items.credibility_basis: Community-driven GitHub resource (1316 stars) but authored for educational purposes; lacks formal peer review. However, curriculum coverage of LLM agents and benchmarking is directly applicable to SOFAR's pipeline maturation.
